notes: Claude Code: an env block in ~/.claude/settings.json overwrites the same shell variable, and managed settings override both. A managed OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, _PROTOCOL or _HEADERS also removes your local endpoints, so Claude Code keeps sending to your organization's collector. A per-signal *_ENDPOINT overrides the general one. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage#how-managed-settings-lock-the-otlp-destination
`cainary scan` shows which of these your organization sets.
The collector is unauthenticated: any local process can post to it, so the stream shows what was received, and the vendor is inferred from the payload.
On Linux only programs run by your own user can send: connections from another local user are refused.
http/protobuf and gzip are accepted too; gRPC isn't.
If the exporting process uses HTTPS_PROXY, add 127.0.0.1, ::1 and localhost to its NO_PROXY, or the proxy gets the request instead of this collector.
takeover: TLS takeover: read this first.
Nothing is forwarded. While this runs, your organization's collector receives nothing from this machine, and every other request to the listed host names fails.
Other programs that talk to these host names will fail their TLS handshake here; that is expected.
The host names below are what you configured here, not an authenticated sender identity.
If the exporting process uses HTTPS_PROXY, add these host names to its NO_PROXY; otherwise the proxy resolves them itself and nothing arrives here.
Your organization's settings choose the format: OTLP over HTTP as JSON or protobuf, gzip or uncompressed, is read; gRPC is not.
1. Point the host names at loopback (add these lines to /etc/hosts as root):
127.0.0.1 otel.example-corp.test
127.0.0.1 logs.example-corp.test
2. Redirect port 443 to <port>, for connections this machine makes to loopback (run these yourself; they are not run for you):
sudo nft add table inet cainary_otel_debug
sudo nft 'add chain inet cainary_otel_debug out { type nat hook output priority -100 ; }'
sudo nft add rule inet cainary_otel_debug out oifname lo ip daddr 127.0.0.1 tcp dport 443 redirect to :<port>
3. Trust the certificate, for the exporting process only (never disable certificate verification):
Claude Code: env NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<ca-dir>/otel-debug-ca.pem claude
Codex: set SSL_CERT_FILE=<ca-dir>/otel-debug-ca.pem or CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE=<ca-dir>/otel-debug-ca.pem for the codex process (see its documentation for which it honors)
Certificate SHA-256: <sha256>

4. Start the exporting process after this certificate is published, and restart it after every run of this program: each run creates a new CA. Deleting the file does not revoke trust a process already loaded; `cainary-otel-debug --delete-ca` removes the file.
Undo: remove the /etc/hosts lines, stop this program, and remove the redirect:
sudo nft delete table inet cainary_otel_debug

The restriction to these names is enforced by this program: it issues certificates only for them and completes a handshake only for them. The certificate also carries name constraints, but those cover subdomains and depend on the client enforcing them. Its key exists only in this process's memory, and it is never installed in a system trust store.
